note: Single copy source for the exploration view. A and B share the solid dashboard treatment. Layout and data stay identical.

optionA.name: Option 1 · Single Blue
optionA.philosophy: One blue family, ordered by alternating lightness so adjacent series stay distinguishable. Comparison is a lighter, desaturated blue — not grey.
optionA.whyItWorks: A single hue keeps the dashboard calm and enterprise. Alternating lightness is what separates six series — not extra colours.
optionA.whyForMaropost: Closest to today's identity. Review this when the question is “can one blue family carry every chart?”
optionA.tradeoff: With many overlapping lines, readers lean on labels and lightness more than hue.
optionA.figmaDescription: Monochromatic blues with alternating lightness. Lead slot is the enterprise blue; comparison is a lighter desaturated blue, not grey.
optionA.vsToday: Same chart treatment as the current dashboard. Only the series, comparison, and axis ramp colours change.

optionB.name: Option 2 · Multi Colour
optionB.philosophy: A fixed categorical order — blue, orange, teal, red, deep blue, green — so the same channel keeps the same colour on every chart.
optionB.whyItWorks: Hue carries category. Channel colours stay stable from the line chart to the donut.
optionB.whyForMaropost: Strongest when several families share one chart — channels, campaigns, segments.
optionB.tradeoff: Furthest from an all-blue identity. New metrics must keep the fixed slot order.
optionB.figmaDescription: Categorical palette drawn from the supplied blue, orange, teal, red, deep-blue, and green family. Same category, same colour.
optionB.vsToday: Same chart treatment as the current dashboard. Only the series, comparison, and axis ramp colours change.
